_comment: Where the mines' monsters and their drop rates are read from.
TWO PAGES, TWO HALVES. The Monsters page has a table per family — which
variants exist and which biome each lives in. `Template:MonsterDrops` has the
drop table, with rates, as one `#switch` on the monster's name.
COSMETIC DROPS ARE GATED. Every family drops a pet skin at 5%, and a hat, and
sometimes sunglasses — but only once the Friend-Shaped perk is unlocked. The
drop shape has nowhere to put that condition, so those are excluded from
`drops` and the monster carries a `perk_gated_drops` gap. An unconditional
'5% pet skin' would be a wrong number, and a wrong number is worse than a
named absence.
WHY THE NAME IS BUILT RATHER THAN READ. The Name column under 'Rock Clods'
says `Rock`, `Blue`, `Green` — it is a variant label, and the family lives in
the section heading. The two are put back together, except where the variant
already carries the family word ('Cool Sapling'), which the same page also
does. The drop table is keyed by the `{{MonsterDrops|…}}` argument instead,
because that is the one value on a row that is complete on its own.
THE MIMIC IS IN EVERY BIOME. Its row says `{{BiomesQuick|All Monster}}`, and
the build writes that out as all five biome ids rather than leaving the list
empty. An empty list reads exactly like 'we do not know which', and those two
must never look the same. Writing it out is safe here because the biome list
is curated in this repo — 'all' cannot quietly come to mean 'all but the one
added last week'.
_incomplete_comment: The Mimic's drop table lists a hat and then links away: what it drops
depends on which biome it was fed in, and that lives on its own page. A
one-line drop list and a genuinely one-drop monster look identical in the
output, so the pointer is detected and the record carries a `drops` gap.
